# Aver.Email

- Try live now: https://www.aver.email
- Demo video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=xL3NfS8PrGw

**Aver.Email** 📧 is a **trustless, privacy-friendly email verification and attestation protocol**. 🔐

It allows users to prove the authenticity of their emails in a completely private manner, without revealing sensitive information.

On Aver.Email, users can upload email files (.eml) and verify their authenticity using DKIM signatures, then extract specific data using customizable regex templates—all processed in a secure Nautilus enclave. Verification templates can be built easily as per custom requirements, and attestation can be done permissionlessly.

With this verification capability, email becomes more than just communication—it becomes a source of cryptographically signed truth. 

You can read more about this project in [ABOUT.md](./ABOUT.md).

## Project structure

- `frontend`: Next.js 15 + React 19 + Tailwind CSS + Framer Motion
- `backend`: Rust-based [Nautilus server](./src/nautilus-server/src/apps/aver-email/) in a Trusted Execution Environment (TEE)
- `storage`: Verification templates are stored on Walrus as an immutable source of truth
- `nautilus`: Nautilus framework for secure and verifiable off-chain computation on Sui

## Nautilus

[aver-email Nautilus app](./src/nautilus-server/src/apps/aver-email/) follows Nautilus structure closely. It is fully implemented in Rust.

In Nautilus, following actions are taken.
- DKIM signature(s) verification
- regex template(s) validation

**About Nautilus:** Nautilus is a framework for **secure and verifiable off-chain computation on Sui**. For full product details, see the [Nautilus documentation](https://docs.sui.io/concepts/cryptography/nautilus).

[expose_enclave.sh](./expose_enclave.sh) needs to be updated with secrets:

```
API_KEY="abc"
FRONTEND_URL="https://www.aver.email"
```

[run.sh](./src/nautilus-server/run.sh) can be used as it is as it has already been configured for allowed endpoints.

## Nautilus deployment proof

The server has been run in an enclave and successfully served `process_data` request. We can show to judges upon requests.

For demo, the server is deployed on Railway EC2.

```shell
[ec2-user@ip-172-31-40-29 aver-email]$ cat out/nitro.pcrs
b6a618b9273b2f2309e36d0b154990f617c196c291bded3196bcb6527d0922b23a2936d9491e84a356e44cbb1d7a1da9 PCR0
b6a618b9273b2f2309e36d0b154990f617c196c291bded3196bcb6527d0922b23a2936d9491e84a356e44cbb1d7a1da9 PCR1
21b9efbc184807662e966d34f390821309eeac6802309798826296bf3e8bec7c10edb30948c90ba67310f7b964fc500a PCR2
```
